events.title: Battle of Issus
events.text: In November, Alexander defeats the Persian king Darius III and opens the road to Syria.

events.title: Damascus taken
events.text: Alexander's general Parmenion seizes the Persian treasure and baggage left at Damascus.

events.title: Arwad surrenders
events.text: At Marathus, Prince Straton crowns Alexander with a golden crown and hands over Arwad and its mainland towns.

events.title: Fleets change sides
events.text: King Gerostratus of Arwad and the kings of Byblos and Sidon bring their warships over to Alexander.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: After seven months, Tyre falls; thousands are killed and some thirty thousand people are sold into slavery.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Gaza holds out for two months before Alexander takes it and marches on Egypt.

events.title: Ptolemy takes Syria
events.text: Ptolemy, satrap of Egypt, sends his general Nicanor to occupy Syria and Phoenicia.

events.title: Antigonus builds fleets
events.text: Antigonus besieges Tyre and builds warships in the Phoenician yards at Tripolis, Byblos and Sidon.

events.title: Battle of Gaza
events.text: Ptolemy and Seleucus defeat Antigonus's son Demetrius; Seleucus returns to Babylon.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: Off Cyprus, Demetrius destroys Ptolemy's fleet; Antigonus and Demetrius take the title of king.

events.title: Syria divided
events.text: After Antigonus dies at Ipsus, Seleucus takes the north and Ptolemy the south, along the Eleutherus river.

events.title: Antioch founded
events.text: Seleucus founds Antioch on the Orontes, the future capital of his dynasty.

events.title: Seleucia Pieria
events.text: Seleucus founds the port of Seleucia at the mouth of the Orontes.

events.title: Apamea's elephants
events.text: Apamea becomes the Seleucid army base, stabling the war elephants that came from India.

events.title: Laodicea founded
events.text: Seleucus founds Laodicea by the Sea, a port just north of Arwad's coast.

events.title: Cyprus is Ptolemaic
events.text: Ptolemy takes Cyprus; it stays in his family's hands for more than two centuries.

events.title: First Syrian War
events.text: Ptolemy II's troops seize Damascus; Antiochus I drives them out.

events.title: Arwad's era begins
events.text: Arwad becomes a free city and starts dating its coins by its own era, from the autumn of 259 BC.

events.title: A royal wedding
events.text: Ptolemy II's daughter Berenice marries Antiochus II, closing the Second Syrian War.

events.title: Ptolemy III in Antioch
events.text: In the Third Syrian War, Ptolemy III enters Antioch and takes Seleucia Pieria.

events.title: Right of asylum
events.text: Arwad backs Seleucus II against his brother Antiochus Hierax and wins the right to shelter fugitives.

events.title: Antiochus repulsed
events.text: The young Antiochus III attacks Ptolemaic Coele-Syria through the Beqaa valley and is turned back.

events.title: Seleucia retaken
events.text: Antiochus III recaptures Seleucia Pieria; the Ptolemaic governor Theodotus hands him Tyre and Ptolemais.

events.title: Alliance at Marathus
events.text: Arwad's envoys ask Antiochus III for an alliance; he grants it and reconciles islanders and mainlanders.

events.title: Battle of Raphia
events.text: Ptolemy IV's seventy-three African elephants and Egyptian phalanx defeat Antiochus III's army of 102 elephants.

events.title: Battle of Panium
events.text: Antiochus III defeats the Ptolemaic general Scopas; Coele-Syria and Phoenicia become Seleucid.

events.title: Hannibal at Tyre
events.text: Exiled from Carthage, Hannibal lands at Tyre, Carthage's mother city, and joins Antiochus III.

events.title: Peace of Apamea
events.text: Beaten by Rome, Antiochus III gives up Asia Minor, his fleet and his war elephants.

events.title: Maccabean revolt
events.text: In Judaea, Mattathias and his sons rise against Antiochus IV's ban on Jewish worship.

events.title: Elephants hamstrung
events.text: Roman envoys have the Seleucid elephants at Apamea crippled; their leader is murdered at Laodicea.

events.title: Marathus destroyed
events.text: Arwad bribes a royal minister, then storms and destroys its old rival Marathus.

events.title: Two crowns in Antioch
events.text: Ptolemy VI enters Antioch and is hailed king of Asia, but dies of wounds weeks later.

events.title: A letter from Rome
events.text: Rome writes to kings and cities, Arwad among them, asking them to leave Judaea in peace.

events.title: Tyre is free
events.text: Tyre breaks away from the Seleucids and begins its own era of autonomy.

events.title: Dura falls
events.text: The Parthians take the Euphrates fortress of Dura-Europos.

events.title: Sidon is free
events.text: Sidon becomes a free city and starts dating by its own era.

events.title: Tripolis is free
events.text: Tripolis, founded by Arwad, Tyre and Sidon together, begins its own era.

events.title: Nabataeans in Damascus
events.text: The Damascenes invite the Nabataean king Aretas III to rule their city.

events.title: Tigranes takes Syria
events.text: Tigranes the Great of Armenia takes over the remains of the Seleucid kingdom.

events.title: The Golan annexed
events.text: The Hasmonean king Alexander Jannaeus takes the Golan for Judaea.

events.title: A last Seleucid
events.text: After Lucullus defeats Tigranes, Antiochus XIII returns to Antioch.

events.title: Pirates swept away
events.text: Pompey clears the Cilician pirates from the sea; Arwad had refused to join them.

events.title: Syria becomes Roman
events.text: Pompey refuses to restore the Seleucids and makes Syria a province; Arwad keeps its era.
